world.title: Carney urges Alberta voters to reject separation process in Oct. 19 vote
world.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney urged Alberta voters to reject a step toward separation, warning at a Calgary rally that unnamed forces outside Canada were trying to “break” the country. Canada and the United States are locked in a trade dispute, and President Donald Trump has threatened to make Canada the 51st sta
world.content: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney urged Alberta voters to reject a step toward separation, warning at a Calgary rally that unnamed forces outside Canada were trying to “break” the country. Canada and the United States are locked in a trade dispute, and President Donald Trump has threatened to make Canada the 51st state. Carney did not name Washington in his speech. Alberta’s Oct. 19 ballot is nonbinding: voters will decide whether to start the legal process toward a later, binding independence referendum, not whether to leave Canada immediately. The ballot also includes nine other questions. Alberta Premier Danielle Smith says she wants the province to remain in Canada but supports those nine proposals; Carney has urged voters to reject them as well. Polling cited in the articles shows most Albertans favor staying in Canada, while separatist organizers say they expect stronger support than polls suggest.

world.title: Illinois teen charged after alleged Hindu temple shooting plot foiled
world.summary: Illinois authorities say police arrested Alexandros Paporakis, 19, on Oct. 11 after a co-worker alerted them to an alleged plan to attack a Hindu temple in Aurora, near Chicago. Prosecutors allege Paporakis drove to the temple with a rifle that jammed when he tried to fire it, then went home and contacted the co-worker
world.content: Illinois authorities say police arrested Alexandros Paporakis, 19, on Oct. 11 after a co-worker alerted them to an alleged plan to attack a Hindu temple in Aurora, near Chicago. Prosecutors allege Paporakis drove to the temple with a rifle that jammed when he tried to fire it, then went home and contacted the co-worker, who alerted police. A search of Paporakis’ home turned up a rifle, loaded magazines, hundreds of rounds of ammunition, body armor and an eight-page document that investigators say contained white-supremacist ideas and references to violence against people of Indian descent. Police have not publicly identified the temple they believe he targeted, though U.S. Representative Raja Krishnamoorthi said he and his family worship there and were there that day. A judge ordered Paporakis held before trial. He is scheduled to return to court on Oct. 30 as investigators continue reviewing the case.
world.image_alt: Illinois teen charged after alleged Hindu temple shooting plot foiled

world.title: Ukraine’s Patriot interceptor stocks run dry as Trump-Zelensky dispute deepens
world.summary: Ukraine has exhausted its stock of U.S.-made Patriot interceptor missiles, CNN reported Thursday, citing a person familiar with the matter, leaving the country with fewer defenses against Russian ballistic missile attacks. During an Oct. 14 attack, Russian missiles hit three power plants in Kyiv and energy infrastructu
world.content: Ukraine has exhausted its stock of U.S.-made Patriot interceptor missiles, CNN reported Thursday, citing a person familiar with the matter, leaving the country with fewer defenses against Russian ballistic missile attacks. During an Oct. 14 attack, Russian missiles hit three power plants in Kyiv and energy infrastructure in Kharkiv; four people were killed and 25 injured in Kyiv. President Donald Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky are at odds over Ukraine’s strikes on Russian oil refineries and Trump’s decision to lift sanctions on Russian diesel exports. Zelensky said he felt betrayed and vowed to continue the attacks; Washington has pressed Kyiv to stop. Two European officials told CNN that U.S. agencies warned they could suspend European-funded purchases of U.S. weapons for Ukraine and intelligence sharing. Trump has said intelligence sharing continues. Ukraine also reported disruptions to Starshield, SpaceX’s military satellite service, that affected military operations. Ukrainian officials said the service had resumed but was not fully restored. Zelensky renewed his request for more Patriot interceptors on Wednesday, but no delivery date has been confirmed.
world.image_alt: Ukraine’s Patriot interceptor stocks run dry as Trump-Zelensky dispute deepens

world.title: NATO source says Russian drones hit tankers as Black Sea attacks spread
world.summary: A NATO military source said Russian drones caused fires on two tankers near Romania, while seven sailors remained missing after the attack on the San Marino-flagged Wine Trader. Romanian President Nicușor Dan confirmed that drones hit the Wine Trader and the Comoros-flagged Yara J but declined to say who launched them;
world.content: A NATO military source said Russian drones caused fires on two tankers near Romania, while seven sailors remained missing after the attack on the San Marino-flagged Wine Trader. Romanian President Nicușor Dan confirmed that drones hit the Wine Trader and the Comoros-flagged Yara J but declined to say who launched them; five of the Wine Trader’s 12 crew members were rescued. The ships were near the Sulina Canal, a Danube outlet used for Ukrainian shipping after Russian attacks on Ukraine’s Black Sea ports. Romania continued its search in dangerous conditions. The NATO source attributed the attacks to Russia, while Romanian officials said an investigation was underway. NATO also said two other vessels had been targeted overnight: the Marshall Islands-flagged bulk carrier Sea Destiny in Romanian waters and the Tanzanian-flagged tanker Dania J at Ukraine’s Izmail port. At least five other cargo vessels had been hit near Romania and Bulgaria in the preceding 10 days, with at least 23 sailors reported missing or dead. NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte said the alliance would adjust its deterrence and defense posture; a NATO official said the North Atlantic Council would discuss the attacks next week. Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev said EU leaders would discuss a proposed moratorium on attacks against civilian ships.
world.image_alt: NATO source says Russian drones hit tankers as Black Sea attacks spread

world.title: Reuters says White House ordered limits on Ukraine
world.summary: The White House ordered a slowdown of SpaceX’s Starshield, the U.S. government-controlled military satellite service Ukraine uses for battlefield communications and drone operations, Reuters reported Friday, citing two U.S. officials and one Western official. Pentagon leaders received a message to slow the service. A s
world.content: The White House ordered a slowdown of SpaceX’s Starshield, the U.S. government-controlled military satellite service Ukraine uses for battlefield communications and drone operations, Reuters reported Friday, citing two U.S. officials and one Western official. Pentagon leaders received a message to slow the service. A senior U.S. official said President Donald Trump did not make the request; the White House did not answer whether another administration official issued it. SpaceX, the Pentagon and Ukraine’s embassy in Washington did not respond to requests for comment. Ukrainian officials said the restrictions disrupted strike missions and interceptor drones. A Ukrainian Defense Ministry official said Thursday that terminals worked in motion only at speeds up to 160 km/h. The reported order followed U.S. pressure on Kyiv to stop attacks on Russian refineries. At an Oct. 9 meeting in Miami, U.S. representatives expressed frustration with Ukraine’s continued strikes, according to a person familiar with the meeting. A senior Ukrainian official said Kyiv sought answers from the White House, State Department and Pentagon and was told the decision came from the White House.
world.image_alt: Reuters says White House ordered limits on Ukraine

world.title: French school protests deepen as police injuries and arrests mount
world.summary: French high school protests over teacher shortages, crowded classrooms, deteriorating buildings and long school days have spread beyond Paris, with blockades and demonstrations entering a fourth week. The government reported injuries to 248 students, 937 police and gendarmes, and 149 education workers; Interior Ministe
world.content: French high school protests over teacher shortages, crowded classrooms, deteriorating buildings and long school days have spread beyond Paris, with blockades and demonstrations entering a fourth week. The government reported injuries to 248 students, 937 police and gendarmes, and 149 education workers; Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said police had used crowd-control weapons at least 18,000 times. A 15-year-old student lost a hand after a police stun grenade exploded during a protest in Lens. Justice Ministry figures showed 7,950 people had been held in police custody by the evening of Oct. 13, including 6,773 minors; 2,735 faced legal proceedings. Authorities are investigating 36 allegations of police misconduct, and a police union has filed a complaint accusing the state of endangering officers. President Emmanuel Macron has asked his government to provide concrete answers in the coming weeks, while officials have begun assigning substitute teachers. Unions, students and Yellow Vest activists are preparing demonstrations for Saturday, Oct. 17; Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has accused France Unbowed of exploiting student anger for electoral advantage ahead of next spring’s presidential election.
world.image_alt: French school protests deepen as police injuries and arrests mount

world.title: Albanian protesters break into economy ministry as unrest spreads
world.summary: Protesters broke into Albania’s Economy and Innovation Ministry office late Thursday, ransacked rooms and removed furniture and equipment. The Central Election Commission building was also damaged on the third day of anti-government unrest. The demonstrations began with students protesting university conditions and cos
world.content: Protesters broke into Albania’s Economy and Innovation Ministry office late Thursday, ransacked rooms and removed furniture and equipment. The Central Election Commission building was also damaged on the third day of anti-government unrest. The demonstrations began with students protesting university conditions and costs, then widened into demands for Prime Minister Edi Rama’s resignation over corruption allegations and opposition to a luxury coastal resort project linked to Jared Kushner. On Thursday, protests and clashes spread beyond Tirana to smaller cities, including Shkodra and Korçë, as students joined university boycotts. In Tirana, police used water cannon and tear gas while protesters attacked public and commercial property. Protest groups set a deadline of 1 p.m. local time for Rama to resign; he rejected the demand and blamed political opponents for the violence. Police chief Skender Hita said 71 officers had been injured, while hospitals treated 89 people after Wednesday’s unrest; four officers and two protesters remained hospitalized, including one officer in intensive care. The opposition Democratic Party has called for a caretaker government ahead of early elections, and protest organizer Mateo Yskollari said demonstrators would return to the square daily.
world.image_alt: Albanian protesters break into economy ministry as unrest spreads

world.title: Israel says Gaza commercial imports halted as merchants and Hamas dispute fees
world.summary: Israel said commercial shipments into Gaza had stopped because merchants suspended coordination over alleged Hamas fees and demands that they conduct 30% of sales in cash. Hamas denied imposing taxes, saying the 10,000-shekel payment was a voluntary contribution to a relief fund and that it encouraged cash transactions
world.content: Israel said commercial shipments into Gaza had stopped because merchants suspended coordination over alleged Hamas fees and demands that they conduct 30% of sales in cash. Hamas denied imposing taxes, saying the 10,000-shekel payment was a voluntary contribution to a relief fund and that it encouraged cash transactions because of a severe cash shortage. The halt cuts off a key source of food and other goods for roughly 2.1 million people in Gaza, where aid agencies typically bring staples such as flour while private traders supply perishables including fruit and meat. Aid workers warn that relief organizations alone cannot meet people’s needs and that reduced commercial supplies could make goods less affordable. Nahed Sheheiber, head of Gaza’s truckers’ union, disputed Israel’s account, saying Israel imposed the restrictions. He said humanitarian aid and some commercial goods from Egypt were still entering. Israel says aid deliveries continue, while Nickolay Mladenov, the Gaza representative of the US-backed Board of Peace, called for the rapid deployment of a Palestinian technocratic administration and an international stabilization force.
world.image_alt: Israel says Gaza commercial imports halted as merchants and Hamas dispute fees

business.title: Anthropic gives nonprofit researchers employee-level access to assess AI risks
business.summary: Anthropic has given six researchers from the nonprofit Model Evaluation and Threat Research (METR) employee-level access to its systems so they can independently assess the company’s AI models, safety practices and risk management. The arrangement gives METR access broadly comparable to Anthropic’s internal risk team,
business.content: Anthropic has given six researchers from the nonprofit Model Evaluation and Threat Research (METR) employee-level access to its systems so they can independently assess the company’s AI models, safety practices and risk management. The arrangement gives METR access broadly comparable to Anthropic’s internal risk team, and the nonprofit can publish its assessments without Anthropic’s approval, subject to limited redactions. The move implements a proposal CEO Dario Amodei made in a September essay calling for outside evaluators to work inside AI labs. Anthropic is also working with SecureBio and Faculty on more limited reviews, and is in early discussions with other organizations, including Hugging Face. The arrangement gives METR the highest access level in a three-tier system Anthropic is developing; the company may seek redactions for customer data, privileged material and model architecture, but METR can publicly challenge those requests.
business.image_alt: Anthropic gives nonprofit researchers employee-level access to assess AI risks

business.title: Bank of America books $1.2 billion charge as profit falls 17%
business.summary: Bank of America reported third-quarter net income of $6.9 billion, down from $8.3 billion a year earlier, after booking a $1.2 billion charge tied to a $1.21 billion U.S. regulatory penalty for anti-money-laundering and sanctions failures. The bank said the charge would reduce earnings by about 17 cents a share; result
business.content: Bank of America reported third-quarter net income of $6.9 billion, down from $8.3 billion a year earlier, after booking a $1.2 billion charge tied to a $1.21 billion U.S. regulatory penalty for anti-money-laundering and sanctions failures. The bank said the charge would reduce earnings by about 17 cents a share; results also fell short of estimates as trading and investment-banking revenue weakened. The U.S. Treasury said the bank failed to report more than $5 billion in suspicious activity, including about $1 billion flagged as posing national-security or other priority risks. The penalty includes a $750 million civil fine from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, which cited shortcomings identified in a 2024 order. A consent order now requires an independent third party to review past transactions and report previously missed suspicious activity to the Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network.
business.image_alt: Bank of America books $1.2 billion charge as profit falls 17%

business.title: Israeli ad firm linked to zero-click spyware across nearly 200,000 websites and apps
business.summary: Researchers at Citizen Lab, a digital investigations unit at the University of Toronto, say Israeli advertising company Discover-Tech used targeted online ads to help spyware maker Candiru, also known as Integrity Labs, infect devices without users clicking or taking any other action. Their report links the operation t
business.content: Researchers at Citizen Lab, a digital investigations unit at the University of Toronto, say Israeli advertising company Discover-Tech used targeted online ads to help spyware maker Candiru, also known as Integrity Labs, infect devices without users clicking or taking any other action. Their report links the operation to at least 45 devices at Qatari broadcaster Al Jazeera and describes it as the first publicly confirmed use of targeted ads to deliver mercenary spyware. The researchers say Discover-Tech’s Controlium platform profiled and identified users, then enabled spyware delivery when an ad appeared. An analysis of four billion ad-bidding records found the company’s ads on nearly 200,000 websites and apps over four months. After receiving the findings, Google, IAB Europe, Beeswax, Vungle and Eskimi cut off Discover-Tech’s access to their advertising systems. Citizen Lab called on regulators to investigate the companies involved.
business.image_alt: Israeli ad firm linked to zero-click spyware across nearly 200,000 websites and apps

business.title: Fed Chair Warsh offers no rate signal as bets on October hold strengthen
business.summary: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh declined to signal whether the U.S. central bank will raise interest rates at its Oct. 27-28 meeting. Speaking Friday in Bangkok at a discussion with International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva, he said he does not prejudge policy decisions. The Fed raised its be
business.content: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh declined to signal whether the U.S. central bank will raise interest rates at its Oct. 27-28 meeting. Speaking Friday in Bangkok at a discussion with International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva, he said he does not prejudge policy decisions. The Fed raised its benchmark rate by a quarter-point in September, its first increase in three years, and Warsh said the bank remains committed to price stability. This week’s inflation readings exceeded expectations, and traders had been looking for signs of whether another increase was imminent. Warsh said economic developments since September had broadly matched policymakers’ expectations and that central banks in many regions were tightening policy to address inflation. He did not rule out another increase, saying officials would base decisions on economic conditions rather than signal a set course. He also said artificial intelligence investment was boosting demand before its potential medium-term gains in supply and productivity emerge. Its near-term effects on employment remain uncertain, he said. A Federal Reserve task force on productivity and jobs plans a public hearing in the San Francisco Bay Area on Nov. 16 to examine the technology’s effects.
business.image_alt: Fed Chair Warsh offers no rate signal as bets on October hold strengthen

business.title: Healey plans higher UK bank taxes in October budget
business.summary: UK Chancellor John Healey is expected to raise taxes on banks in his Oct. 28 budget, most likely by increasing the sector’s profit surcharge, according to people familiar with the plans. The government is seeking revenue to support households facing higher living costs and shore up public finances after borrowing costs
business.content: UK Chancellor John Healey is expected to raise taxes on banks in his Oct. 28 budget, most likely by increasing the sector’s profit surcharge, according to people familiar with the plans. The government is seeking revenue to support households facing higher living costs and shore up public finances after borrowing costs rose, while avoiding tax increases Labour pledged not to impose. Banks currently pay a 3% surcharge on top of the 25% corporation tax rate; restoring the surcharge to its former 8% level could raise more than £2 billion a year. Healey has not publicly confirmed the measure, and the Treasury declined to comment on the reported plans. He will set out his tax and spending decisions in the Oct. 28 budget.
business.image_alt: Healey plans higher UK bank taxes in October budget

business.title: Anthropic IPO investors cut valuation expectations as revenue growth slows
business.summary: Some investors are reportedly considering a valuation of about $1.5 trillion for Anthropic’s planned initial public offering, down from as much as $2 trillion previously discussed. Investors raised concerns about slowing quarterly revenue growth after the developer of the Claude artificial-intelligence model reported $
business.content: Some investors are reportedly considering a valuation of about $1.5 trillion for Anthropic’s planned initial public offering, down from as much as $2 trillion previously discussed. Investors raised concerns about slowing quarterly revenue growth after the developer of the Claude artificial-intelligence model reported $16.8 billion in third-quarter revenue, up about 45% from the previous quarter. Anthropic presented its results to prospective investors at its San Francisco headquarters on Wednesday. It reported a second consecutive quarter of adjusted profit, positive free cash flow and an 11% adjusted operating margin. The company has not yet published a full IPO prospectus. Revenue grew more slowly than in the previous quarter, when it more than doubled from the first quarter. Anthropic is still preparing for a November listing, with formal investor marketing potentially starting the week of Nov. 9, according to people familiar with the plans cited by Bloomberg News. The valuation remains under discussion, and the schedule could change.
business.image_alt: Anthropic IPO investors cut valuation expectations as revenue growth slows

business.title: Ukraine’s Starshield service restored after restrictions disrupt military drone missions
business.summary: SpaceX’s military-grade Starshield satellite service returned to normal capacity in Ukraine on Thursday, Oct. 15, after speed restrictions disrupted drone operations and other missions, Ukrainian officials and military personnel said. The disruption affected terminals moving faster than 100 miles per hour, and some uni
business.content: SpaceX’s military-grade Starshield satellite service returned to normal capacity in Ukraine on Thursday, Oct. 15, after speed restrictions disrupted drone operations and other missions, Ukrainian officials and military personnel said. The disruption affected terminals moving faster than 100 miles per hour, and some units reported losing connectivity at lower speeds. A Ukrainian commander said drones and other systems were lost when communications failed. Ukraine uses SpaceX connectivity for real-time communications, drone control and air defense. SpaceX chief executive Elon Musk said the U.S. government owns and controls Starshield and that the U.S. military and ultimately the president decide its limits. A senior U.S. official separately told Business Insider that President Donald Trump had not requested restrictions. Who ordered the restrictions remains disputed. Reuters sources cited by Estonian business outlet Äripäev said the order came from the White House, while a senior U.S. official said the president had not requested the measure. Ukraine’s Defense Ministry said it was investigating the circumstances. Ukrainian units reported restored service, while Ukraine’s army was preparing backup communications.
business.image_alt: Ukraine’s Starshield service restored after restrictions disrupt military drone missions

business.title: IMF warns debt-funded AI investment risks financial turmoil as markets rebound
business.summary: The International Monetary Fund warned that debt-financed artificial intelligence investment could unsettle financial markets if returns fall short, as U.S. stocks recovered and South Korean shares rebounded after a multiday technology selloff. The selloff reflected investor concerns that high borrowing costs and uncer
business.content: The International Monetary Fund warned that debt-financed artificial intelligence investment could unsettle financial markets if returns fall short, as U.S. stocks recovered and South Korean shares rebounded after a multiday technology selloff. The selloff reflected investor concerns that high borrowing costs and uncertain profits could constrain the data-centre expansion underpinning the AI boom. On Friday, South Korea’s Kospi rose 2.05% and the Kosdaq gained 4%, after U.S. stocks recovered some losses in Thursday trading. IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said AI could add about half a percentage point to annual global growth over the next decade, but warned that borrowing and financial links among technology companies could spread losses beyond the sector if earnings disappoint. Credit concerns have focused on CoreWeave, a U.S. provider of AI cloud-computing capacity. Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang dismissed the idea that Nvidia would need to rescue the company, while investors remained focused on CoreWeave’s credit risk.
business.image_alt: IMF warns debt-funded AI investment risks financial turmoil as markets rebound

science.title: Sydney PhD student maps Martian soils for future food production
science.summary: A PhD student at the University of Sydney has produced the first comprehensive classification system and map of Martian soils, providing a framework for scientists to assess which materials could support future food production on Mars. The classification could also help researchers identify promising locations for expl
science.content: A PhD student at the University of Sydney has produced the first comprehensive classification system and map of Martian soils, providing a framework for scientists to assess which materials could support future food production on Mars. The classification could also help researchers identify promising locations for exploration and habitation, according to the project summary.
science.image_alt: Sydney PhD student maps Martian soils for future food production

science.title: Researchers turn atomically thin crystal into transistor with integrated components
science.summary: Researchers describe an atomically thin material that can be converted into crystals with different electronic properties. They also demonstrate a transistor made from a single two-dimensional crystal, with built-in insulation and electrical contacts. Conventional transistors combine separate semiconductor, insulating
science.content: Researchers describe an atomically thin material that can be converted into crystals with different electronic properties. They also demonstrate a transistor made from a single two-dimensional crystal, with built-in insulation and electrical contacts. Conventional transistors combine separate semiconductor, insulating and metallic materials, which become harder to integrate at atomic scales. A separate report describes a monolayer van der Waals kagome lattice for high-temperature flat-band physics.
science.image_alt: Researchers turn atomically thin crystal into transistor with integrated components

science.title: Astronomers map white dwarfs’ colors, identifying green and salmon-pink stars
science.summary: A study published in RAS Techniques and Instruments describes how stellar remnants known as white dwarfs can appear green, salmon-pink, yellow or other colors, not just white or blue. Astronomers converted stellar spectra into colors as human eyes would perceive them because the stars are too distant for the colors of
science.content: A study published in RAS Techniques and Instruments describes how stellar remnants known as white dwarfs can appear green, salmon-pink, yellow or other colors, not just white or blue. Astronomers converted stellar spectra into colors as human eyes would perceive them because the stars are too distant for the colors of their disks to be seen directly. The team identifies WD J1330+6435 as a chartreuse-green example and WD J1011+2845, 48 light-years away, as a likely record-setting salmon-pink star. In a nearby sample, five of 151 white dwarfs had unusual colors; the researchers estimate that roughly one in 30 white dwarfs may be unusually colored. The median color of the nearby sample is white, not blue.
science.image_alt: Astronomers map white dwarfs’ colors, identifying green and salmon-pink stars

science.title: Osaka team develops compact chip to test samples for life clues
science.summary: An international team led by Japan’s Osaka University has developed a microchip sensor that distinguishes the mirror-image L and D forms of amino acids, potential clues to a sample’s origins. The device combines a gap between two gold nanowires with machine learning to read electrical changes when amino-acid samples to
science.content: An international team led by Japan’s Osaka University has developed a microchip sensor that distinguishes the mirror-image L and D forms of amino acids, potential clues to a sample’s origins. The device combines a gap between two gold nanowires with machine learning to read electrical changes when amino-acid samples touch the sensor. The team reported more than 80% accuracy in distinguishing the forms. Researchers tested it on material from the Murchison meteorite and soil from Chile’s Atacama Desert. Results for major features of amino-acid composition were comparable to those from conventional analysis. The method requires direct contact with a sample and needs further development, including tests of whether its machine-learning system can identify molecules absent from its training data.
science.image_alt: Osaka team develops compact chip to test samples for life clues

science.title: Stanford study details how contact with healthy coral revives bleached fragments
science.summary: A Stanford University study found that bleached coral fragments recovered after brief contact with healthy fragments from the same colony. The researchers found beneficial algae moving into damaged coral within three days. After about a week, some fragments had enough algae to begin recovering without continued contact
science.content: A Stanford University study found that bleached coral fragments recovered after brief contact with healthy fragments from the same colony. The researchers found beneficial algae moving into damaged coral within three days. After about a week, some fragments had enough algae to begin recovering without continued contact. The effect depends on the corals being genetically identical, which limits the method’s use across reefs. Researchers are exploring ways to deliver the beneficial algae without contact between genetically matched corals. Stanford marine biologist Steve Palumbi said the approach cannot prevent the heatwaves that cause bleaching.
science.image_alt: Stanford study details how contact with healthy coral revives bleached fragments

science.title: Polo study finds warming contributed more than El Niño, but did not focus on wind shear
science.summary: Researchers examining Hurricane Polo’s rapid intensification say human-caused warming contributed more than El Niño. Their attribution study examined warm ocean water but did not focus on upper-level wind shear. Polo intensified from a tropical storm to Category 5 in about 24 hours, then weakened before reaching Baja C
science.content: Researchers examining Hurricane Polo’s rapid intensification say human-caused warming contributed more than El Niño. Their attribution study examined warm ocean water but did not focus on upper-level wind shear. Polo intensified from a tropical storm to Category 5 in about 24 hours, then weakened before reaching Baja California Sur. Flooding linked to the storm killed five people in Mexico. The researchers compared conditions in today’s world, about 1.4 degrees Celsius warmer than the preindustrial period, with a hypothetical world without that warming. Two research groups used different methods but reached the same broad conclusion. The rapid study has not undergone peer review. The researchers noted that El Niño can reduce winds that would otherwise weaken Pacific storms, a factor the warm-water analysis did not focus on. Study co-author Daniel Gilford said the team considered other conditions and chose a conservative estimate.
science.image_alt: Polo study finds warming contributed more than El Niño, but did not focus on wind shear

science.title: England declares severe drought in parts of six counties as reservoirs run low
science.summary: The UK government declared a severe drought on Oct. 15 in parts of Cornwall, Devon, Dorset, Somerset, East Sussex and West Sussex after months of low rainfall. More than 80% of England is in drought after the country’s hottest summer on record; southeast and southwest England had their driest April-to-September period
science.content: The UK government declared a severe drought on Oct. 15 in parts of Cornwall, Devon, Dorset, Somerset, East Sussex and West Sussex after months of low rainfall. More than 80% of England is in drought after the country’s hottest summer on record; southeast and southwest England had their driest April-to-September period in more than a century. Two southwest reservoirs serving nearly 400,000 properties were below 20% full, compared with the Environment Agency’s expected level of about 75% for this time of year. The Environment Agency is increasing checks on reservoir and river levels and on businesses that draw water from natural sources, while authorities urge customers to use less water. About 30 million people in England and Wales are covered by hosepipe bans. Three water companies have sought permission to restrict non-essential commercial water use, but the government had not approved the proposed bans.
science.image_alt: England declares severe drought in parts of six counties as reservoirs run low

science.title: New model doubles Thwaites Glacier
science.summary: A revised ice-sheet model estimates that Thwaites Glacier in West Antarctica could add about 3 centimeters to global sea levels by 2100—roughly twice earlier projections—after accounting for ocean water moving beneath the ice. Researchers at the University of California, Irvine, and NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory sai
science.content: A revised ice-sheet model estimates that Thwaites Glacier in West Antarctica could add about 3 centimeters to global sea levels by 2100—roughly twice earlier projections—after accounting for ocean water moving beneath the ice. Researchers at the University of California, Irvine, and NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory said satellite observations show seawater entering and leaving a broad grounding zone with the tides, carrying relatively warm water beneath the glacier. The model projects that rise even without further global warming. The researchers say the glacier’s retreat depends on complex processes that still need direct observation. The team plans to place instruments near Thwaites’ grounding zone in 2028 to measure the water’s movement.

sports.title: McIlroy and Reed mend rift at DP World India Championship
sports.summary: Rory McIlroy and Patrick Reed have repaired their relationship at the DP World India Championship, where McIlroy is also pursuing the Race to Dubai season title. McIlroy shot a two-under 70 in his opening round, four shots behind leader Niklas Nørgaard, while Eugenio Chacarra—second in the season standings—was one shot
sports.content: Rory McIlroy and Patrick Reed have repaired their relationship at the DP World India Championship, where McIlroy is also pursuing the Race to Dubai season title. McIlroy shot a two-under 70 in his opening round, four shots behind leader Niklas Nørgaard, while Eugenio Chacarra—second in the season standings—was one shot off the lead. McIlroy said he played solidly despite missed putting chances and saw the week as a chance to close the gap in the standings before the final two events in the Middle East. The first round remained unfinished after a five-hour weather interruption, with Reed’s opening-round position still undetermined and the leaderboard unsettled.
sports.image_alt: McIlroy and Reed mend rift at DP World India Championship

sports.title: Troy Aikman’s ESPN future uncertain as Joe Buck secures $108 million deal
sports.summary: Hall of Fame quarterback Troy Aikman says he will become a free agent after the NFL season and is weighing his next job, leaving his future with ESPN uncertain as the network prepares to broadcast the February 2027 Super Bowl. Aikman, who earns $18 million a year, said he will work through the season; Joe Buck, his lon
sports.content: Hall of Fame quarterback Troy Aikman says he will become a free agent after the NFL season and is weighing his next job, leaving his future with ESPN uncertain as the network prepares to broadcast the February 2027 Super Bowl. Aikman, who earns $18 million a year, said he will work through the season; Joe Buck, his longtime Monday Night Football partner, has signed a six-year ESPN extension reportedly worth $108 million. Front Office Sports reported friction over the two men’s contracts, including an argument before Monday’s Bills-Rams game that subsided without affecting their broadcast, according to SB Nation. Aikman did not directly confirm the reported dispute, saying there would be a “time and a place” to discuss it. ESPN has not announced a new deal for him, and Aikman said he will see what opportunities emerge after the season.

sports.content: England captain Harry Kane has agreed in principle to extend his Bayern Munich contract through the summer of 2029, keeping the 33-year-old striker at the German club beyond his current deal. Bayern are completing the paperwork, but final details remain unresolved and the agreement has not yet been signed. Kane joined Bayern from Tottenham in 2023 and has scored 154 goals in 156 appearances, helping the club win back-to-back Bundesliga titles. He has said he is happy at the club and wants a positive outcome from the negotiations. Bayern are reportedly aiming to announce the extension before the Ballon d’Or ceremony in London on October 26, where Kane is among the favourites, though the timing depends on settling the remaining details.

sports.title: FIFA president apologises over commercial-rights plan as critics demand answers
sports.summary: FIFA president Gianni Infantino apologised to the governing body’s council on Thursday in Zurich for failing to consult and communicate over FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), an abandoned proposal to give private investors a stake in FIFA’s commercial rights. Infantino said it was a proposal, not a completed deal, intende
sports.content: FIFA president Gianni Infantino apologised to the governing body’s council on Thursday in Zurich for failing to consult and communicate over FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), an abandoned proposal to give private investors a stake in FIFA’s commercial rights. Infantino said it was a proposal, not a completed deal, intended to increase funding for FIFA’s 211 member associations. He promised written answers “in due course”. English Football Association chair and FIFA vice-president Debbie Hewitt said council members still had not received requested FFE documents or answers on the proposal, the decision to suspend US striker Folarin Balogun’s World Cup red-card ban, and FIFA’s Peace Prize for US President Donald Trump. German Football Association president Bernd Neuendorf said FIFA needed a governance overhaul that Infantino could not deliver. Infantino is seeking re-election in March 2027. Opponents must nominate a challenger by 18 November. The council is due to meet again in Doha on 16 December, when Infantino has pledged to provide information on the Balogun case.

sports.title: Conte signals readiness for Manchester United job as Carrick faces pressure

sports.content: Antonio Conte, the former Chelsea, Tottenham and Napoli manager, is willing to take charge of Manchester United if the club dismisses head coach Michael Carrick, with his representatives reported to have renewed contact with the club. United have not opened formal negotiations and remain publicly committed to Carrick, but the 45-year-old is under pressure after his side took six points from their first six Premier League matches and lost 2-0 to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League. Conte has been without a club since leaving Napoli at the end of last season. Football transfer journalist Fabrizio Romano said Conte is open to taking a job mid-season, especially at a historic club seeking to return to the top level, but stressed that no serious discussions with United were underway. Conte’s representatives had also expressed interest in the job during the summer, when United instead appointed Carrick after his interim spell. United travel to Leeds United on Sunday, October 18. Reports say the club has not made Carrick’s job contingent on that match. Julian Nagelsmann and Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler are also among the names linked with the role.

sports.content: Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola said Thursday that Dominik Szoboszlai, Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo could return for Saturday’s Premier League visit to Brentford, but their availability depends on Friday’s training. Isak has a thigh injury, Gakpo an ankle problem and Szoboszlai a hamstring issue; none played in Liverpool’s 6-3 Champions League win over LASK on Wednesday. Liverpool are also short of options with Ryan Gravenberch suspended for one match and Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni still injured. Liverpool sit ninth, one point behind fourth-placed Brentford, who remain unbeaten after six league matches. Iraola said the club would assess the trio after training; they are not expected to start even if fit.

Milwaukee trailed 4-0 after Shohei Ohtani’s three-run homer, but Brewers first baseman Jake
sports.content: The Milwaukee Brewers rallied from a four-run deficit to beat the Los Angeles Dodgers 6-4 in Game 4 on Thursday, completing a four-game National League Championship Series sweep and reaching their first World Series since 1982. Milwaukee trailed 4-0 after Shohei Ohtani’s three-run homer, but Brewers first baseman Jake Bauers’ two-run double and a bases-loaded walk helped tie the game before Garrett Mitchell’s sixth-inning homer put Milwaukee ahead for good. The win ended the Dodgers’ bid for a third straight championship and gave Milwaukee its first National League pennant. The Brewers’ relievers held Los Angeles scoreless over the final seven innings, while David Hamilton added a ninth-inning home run. Milwaukee will host the World Series opener on Oct. 23 against the winner of the American League Championship Series between the Cleveland Guardians and Tampa Bay Rays. Cleveland led that series 2-1 after Game 3 on Thursday; Game 4 is scheduled for Friday, Oct. 16.

sports.content: New Zealand will keep fullback Kalyn Ponga with the squad as he undergoes surgery for a broken left arm and assess whether he can return later in the Rugby League World Cup. Ponga scored twice before leaving injured in the Kiwis’ 24-22 loss to Australia in Thursday’s opener. Ponga broke the radius in his left arm and will remain with the team during his recovery; New Zealand coach Stacey Jones said Keano Kini would likely take his place against the Cook Islands next week. New Zealand can seek permission to add a player if Ponga’s tournament is over, and will also face Fiji in the pool stage.
